newsitem.title: USA: NASA AIMS TO REDUCE AIR ACCIDENTS BY 80PCT BY 2007.
newsitem.headline: NASA AIMS TO REDUCE AIR ACCIDENTS BY 80PCT BY 2007.

text.p: The U.S. space agency unveiled a plan on Wednesday aimed at reducing fatal air accidents by 80 percent over the next decade.

The project, which will be handled by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration and the Federal Aviation Administration, will work with the aviation industry to set up integrated systems to stop accidents at the earliest point in the chain, said NASA's Michael Lewis.

Operating on the theory that accidents are caused by a combination of events, the program's challenge is to craft solutions for entire categories of accidents, not to look at single causes, Lewis said.

Among the broad areas of inquiry that will be part of the program are weather problems, human error, flight-critical systems and information integrity, and system-wide monitoring, modeling and simulation.

As an example, Lewis suggested that the problem of poor visibility of the ground might be addressed by putting a real-time view of the terrain on the pilot's cockpit computer screen, using data from global positioning satellites and other technology.

Lewis, who heads the aviation safety program's office, told industry representatives gathered at NASA headquarters that new and existing technology coupled with more data about aviation accidents could produce the first results by mid-1998.
NASA's initial investment in the safety project is $500 million over the next five years, Lewis said.
